units.translation: c. 〈Parthenian〉 Ancaeus: Aristotle (fr. 530 Rose) says, applying the proverb to Ancaeus, that Ancaeus was fond of farming and planted many vines. When his servant told him that he would die sooner than drink from the fruit of the vine, Ancaeus, when the fruit was ripe, crushed a grape, called the servant, and said that he had lived until the vine bore fruit, and was about to drink. But when the servant said, 'Many things happen between the cup and the lip,' it was reported to him that a boar was ravaging the land; he rushed out against it before drinking and was killed by it. Therefore the proverb prevailed for those who suffer something contrary to expectation. And Pherecydes in the eighth book (3 fr. 36 J.) says that Ancaeus was struck in the thigh by the Calydonian boar and died.

193. But a hired woman: 'thessa' means a female slave. The Athenians also call the poor 'thetes', from 'theteuein' (to serve for hire), because they lack the necessities. And just as 'Kres' has the feminine 'Kressa', so 'thes' has 'thessa'.
